name: Inositol nicotinate (inositol hexanicotinate)
short: Safety data are sparse. A 6-week trial called it well tolerated but noted small rises in liver enzymes without saying in which group; a review of claudication drugs reported minor adverse events.
text: Few safety data specific to inositol nicotinate were found. In a 6-week placebo-controlled trial in people with mild to moderate dyslipidaemia (40 per arm) that compared it with extended-release niacin, inositol hexanicotinate was described as well tolerated; the abstract reports small mean increases (24% to 27%) in liver transaminases without saying in which treatment group or groups they occurred, and reports that a pharmacokinetic substudy in 5 participants showed no evidence of bioavailability. A systematic review of four vasoactive drugs for intermittent claudication, including inositol nicotinate, reported that adverse events were minor for all drugs and included headaches and gastrointestinal difficulties, and that serious adverse events, including cardiovascular events and mortality, were not increased compared with placebo, while cautioning that most studies had a relatively short follow-up; the abstract does not give adverse-event figures for inositol nicotinate separately and says it was left out of the main analyses owing to lack of data. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
